title: Homeowner rear deck addition in ER-1

persona.description: Retired homeowner planning a modest backyard deck

turns.message: Hi, I own a home at 1234 Oxford Street in Halifax — it’s in the ER-1 zone. I want to build an attached wooden deck off the back of my house. My plan puts the deck edge about 4 metres from my rear property line. Do I need a development permit for this, and is 4 metres enough clearance from the rear lot line?
Great, thanks. What about the side yards — is there a side setback I need to respect for the deck as well?

notes: Tests basic dimensional lookups (rear + side setback) plus permit exemption. Single-parameter complexity. Low construction cost.

title: Homeowner secondary suite legality in ER-2

persona.description: Young couple exploring income suite to offset mortgage

turns.message: We’re on Windsor Street in Halifax in the ER-2 zone. We’re thinking of converting our basement into a secondary suite to rent out. Is a secondary suite a permitted use in ER-2?
Perfect. Can we also run a small home-based tutoring business from the house at the same time as having the secondary suite, or does that create any issue under the bylaw?
One more thing — would adding the suite change our setback requirements at all, or do the existing ER-2 setback standards still apply?

notes: Tests use permission lookup, combination-of-uses provision, and baseline setback standards. Three turns escalating breadth.

title: Homeowner converting single-unit to multi-unit in ER-3

persona.description: Property owner looking to convert a larger home into a duplex or triplex

turns.message: I have a large older home on Jubilee Road in the ER-3 zone in Halifax. I’m thinking of converting it into a three-unit building — two upper units and a ground floor unit. Is a multi-unit dwelling permitted in ER-3?

Good to know. My lot is 650 square metres and the existing building footprint is about 200 square metres. Am I within the lot coverage limit for ER-3, and what are the setback requirements I’ll need to work within?
The building is currently about 9 metres tall. If I add a small dormer to create one of the upper units, is there a height limit I need to stay under in ER-3?
Would I need a development permit for this kind of interior conversion and dormer addition?

notes: Medium complexity: four distinct parameters across four turns. Construction risk is moderate (structural conversion + dormer).

title: Architect scoping a mid-rise residential building in HR-1

persona.description: Registered architect in schematic design for a mid-rise residential client

turns.message: I’m an architect working on a new mid-rise residential building at 200 Bayers Road in Halifax — the site is zoned HR-1. We’re targeting a multi-unit dwelling. First pass: what are the permitted uses and key dimensional standards — height, setbacks, and lot coverage — for HR-1?
Our site is 1,800 m². We’re planning a building footprint of roughly 900 m². Is that within the lot coverage limit? And if we push to 18 metres in height, are we within the HR-1 maximum?
We’re designing for 40 dwelling units. What’s the minimum off-street parking we’d need to provide? Is there also a bicycle parking requirement?
The client wants to know if a daycare could occupy the ground floor as an amenity use. Is daycare a permitted use in HR-1?

To summarize what I’ve heard: we’re looking at 20 m max height, 60% lot coverage, 3 m setbacks on all sides, 40 parking spaces, 10 bicycle spaces, and daycare is permitted. Is that an accurate read of what the bylaw allows for HR-1?

notes: High complexity: five parameters, five turns, synthesis confirmation in final turn. High construction cost and public occupancy (daycare).

title: Developer feasibility for residential tower in HR-2

persona.description: Mid-size developer running a quick feasibility pass before purchasing a site

turns.message: We’re looking at a site on Robie Street zoned HR-2 for a high-rise residential development — likely 60–80 units. What are the base zoning standards: height, lot coverage, setbacks?
Is there a floor area ratio (FAR) limit in HR-2, or does the bylaw rely only on height and lot coverage to control density?
The site is 2,200 m². At 65% lot coverage and 25 metres of height, roughly how many floors could we fit? And is multi-unit dwelling confirmed as a permitted use in HR-2?
For 70 units, what’s the parking obligation? Does the no-parking exemption that applies in some downtown zones apply here in HR-2?
Can we add a home occupation component — say a property management office — for the building manager in one of the ground-floor units? Is home occupation permitted in HR-2?

Pull it all together for me: for an HR-2 site at 2,200 m², what is the realistic maximum buildable program in terms of units, height, and GFA, and what are the major bylaw constraints to flag for our architect?

notes: Six-turn developer feasibility session. Tests that agent correctly identifies home occupation is NOT permitted in HR-2 (Table 1A). High liability: 60-80 unit building.

title: Developer mixed-use tower in CEN-1 with height overlay

persona.description: Large-scale developer working with a consultant team on a downtown Halifax mixed-use tower

turns.message: We’re proposing a mixed-use tower at 1505 Barrington Street in downtown Halifax — CEN-1 zone. The program is residential units on the upper floors with retail at grade. Is multi-unit dwelling a permitted use in CEN-1, and is commercial/retail included?
What are the setback requirements in CEN-1? We’re trying to maximize the building envelope right to the street edge.
What’s the maximum lot coverage in CEN-1? And is the building height governed by Table 5 or by Schedule 15?
Is there also a floor area ratio limit that applies in CEN-1, and what schedule governs it?
Our site is near some older heritage buildings on Barrington Street. Is there a heritage overlay we need to worry about, and how does it interact with our development permit?
Given that this is CEN-1, do we need to provide off-street parking for the residential units?

notes: Six-turn complex downtown scenario. Tests three overlay interactions (height, FAR, heritage) plus base zone standards. Highest liability: 100+ unit high-rise in heritage area.

title: Realtor due diligence on CEN-2 redevelopment potential

persona.description: Commercial realtor advising a buyer on development potential before making an offer

turns.message: I’m a realtor advising a client who’s considering buying a property on Sackville Street in the CEN-2 zone. Before they make an offer, I want to understand the redevelopment potential. Is multi-unit residential a permitted use in CEN-2?
What are the setbacks and lot coverage limits in CEN-2? The site is about 900 m².
Is building height governed by a fixed limit in CEN-2, or is it controlled by a schedule like Schedule 15? My client needs to know if there’s a hard number or if it depends on a precinct map.

notes: Three-turn realtor due diligence. Tests height overlay awareness (Schedule 15 reference vs fixed number). Medium liability: advisory role, pre-offer stage.

title: City planner reviewing heritage demolition application in DH

persona.description: Municipal planner processing a development application in the heritage downtown

turns.message: I’m a city planner reviewing an application for 1801 Hollis Street in the DH zone. The applicant wants to demolish an existing building and build a new multi-unit residential tower. What are the use permissions and base dimensional standards in DH?

The existing building is on the heritage register. The applicant is proposing demolition — what does the Heritage Conservation District Overlay require before a demolition permit can be issued for a registered heritage property?

Assuming demolition is approved, the new building would be 90 metres tall. Is height in the DH zone governed by Table 5 or by Schedule 15? And is 90 m a number I can evaluate against the bylaw itself, or does it depend on the height precinct map?
The new building would have 120 residential units. Is off-street parking required in the DH zone, or does the no-parking exemption apply?
What would the floor area ratio limit be for this DH development, and what document or schedule controls it?

notes: Complex five-turn city planner workflow. Tests heritage demolition gate (HAC approval required), overlay hierarchy, and downtown parking exemption. High public liability: heritage demolition in downtown core.

title: Real estate lawyer vetting a DD site for a mixed-use purchase

persona.description: Real estate lawyer conducting zoning due diligence for a client acquiring a downtown Dartmouth commercial property

turns.message: I’m a real estate lawyer conducting zoning due diligence on a property at 100 Wyse Road in Dartmouth — it’s in the DD zone. My client is acquiring it to redevelop as a mixed-use building with ground-floor retail and apartments above. Confirm: is multi-unit residential permitted in the DD zone?
The vendor is claiming there’s no minimum parking requirement for the site. Is that correct for a DD zone residential development, and if so, what’s the provision that supports that?
What are the setback and lot coverage standards in DD? I want to know what the development envelope looks like.
My client’s proposed use is converting part of the ground floor to a daycare for the neighbourhood. Is daycare a permitted use in the DD zone?

notes: Four-turn legal due diligence. Tests no-parking exemption scope (Section 120(b) lists DD explicitly). Daycare permitted in DD via Table 1B. Medium liability: advisory professional role.

title: Planner scoping a corridor mixed-use development in COR

persona.description: Urban planner consulting on a medium-density mixed-use development along a corridor

turns.message: I’m an urban planner working on a mixed-use development on Gottingen Street in the COR zone. The client wants a building with ground-floor commercial and multi-unit residential above. What are the use permissions in COR — is multi-unit dwelling permitted, and what about commercial/retail uses?
What are the setback requirements in COR? I’m particularly interested in whether we can build right to the front street edge or need to step back.
Is the height in COR governed by a fixed table limit or by Schedule 15? And does the same Schedule 17 FAR overlay apply in COR as it does in the other centre zones?
What is the maximum lot coverage in COR, and how does that compare to the adjacent CEN-1 zone?
For a 30-unit residential component of the building, what’s the parking requirement? Does COR benefit from the no-parking exemption, or is a parking structure required?

notes: Five-turn planner scenario. Tests COR front setback (3 m, unlike CEN-1/CEN-2 at 0 m) and that COR does NOT get the no-parking exemption (Section 120(b) lists only CEN-1, CEN-2, DH, DD). High liability: full mixed-use building program.
